title: Galho with Smoked Pork
steps: Cook rice with smoked pork, local greens, ginger and chilli, adding enough water for a porridge-like consistency.
Simmer till everything is soft and the flavours meld.
Serve hot – a comforting one-pot meal popular among Angami and other tribes.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Naga-style khichdi/porridge with smoked pork.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Smoked meat gives the classic flavour.

title: Galho with Vegetables
steps: Cook rice with mixed vegetables, local greens, onion, garlic, ginger and chilli, adding enough water for a porridge-like consistency.
Simmer till everything is soft and the flavours meld.
Serve hot – a comforting one-pot meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of the Naga-style khichdi/porridge.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Hearty and nourishing.

title: Steamed Rice with Boiled Vegetables & Chutney
steps: Steam or boil rice. Separately boil or steam seasonal greens and vegetables with minimal seasoning.
Serve with a fiery Naga chilli or fermented bamboo-shoot chutney.
A simple, everyday start to the day.

fullIngredients.name: Naga chilli or king chilli chutney, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Many Naga households begin the day with plain rice, boiled vegetables and a strong chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fermented or fresh chilli chutneys are essential.

title: Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoot
steps: Boil or simmer the smoked pork until tender. Add fermented or fresh bamboo shoot, chilli and ginger.
Cook till the flavours blend and the gravy is well reduced.
Serve with steamed rice – one of the most iconic Naga dishes.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The smokiness of the pork and the tang of bamboo shoot define the dish.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal spices; the ingredients speak for themselves.

title: Smoked Pork with Axone (Akhuni)
steps: Cook smoked pork with a little water till tender. Add mashed axone, chilli and ginger.
Simmer until the pungent, umami-rich gravy coats the meat.
Serve with rice – a Sümi Naga speciality now loved across the state.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Axone is intensely aromatic (and polarising for newcomers) but deeply flavourful.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Use sparingly at first if unfamiliar.

title: Pork with Anishi
steps: Cook pork till tender. Crumble or break the anishi patties into the pot.
Simmer so the dark, earthy anishi forms a thick gravy with the pork.
Serve with rice – an Ao Naga classic.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Anishi is made by fermenting and smoking taro leaves into dense, coal-like patties.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Gives a unique dark colour and deep flavour.

title: Chicken with Axone
steps: Cook chicken with ginger, garlic and chilli. Add axone and a little water.
Simmer till the chicken is tender and the gravy is rich and aromatic.
Serve with rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A lighter alternative to pork-axone combinations.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Still carries the signature fermented soybean punch.

title: Fish with Bamboo Shoot
steps: Cook the fish gently with bamboo shoot, chilli and ginger.
Simmer till the fish is done and the flavours have blended.
Serve with rice – common in riverine and many tribal households.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bamboo shoot pairs especially well with fish.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can also be cooked inside bamboo tubes for a traditional smoked version.

title: Boiled Yam
steps: Boil or steam yam until soft.
Peel and eat with a sprinkle of salt or a side of chilli chutney.
A simple, filling snack or light meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common everyday snack across many Naga tribes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with tea.

title: Boiled Sweet Potato
steps: Boil or steam sweet potato until soft.
Peel and eat with a sprinkle of salt or a side of chilli chutney.
A simple, filling snack or light meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common everyday snack across many Naga tribes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with tea.

title: Roasted Naga Dal
steps: Dry-roast the dal in a pan until aromatic and slightly browned.
Sprinkle with salt water and stir till the water is absorbed.
Eat as a crunchy, protein-rich snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple roasted bean snack popular in several communities.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Portable and long-lasting.

title: Akibiye
steps: Cook colocasia and bamboo shoot with other available vegetables into a thick gravy.
Season simply with chilli and salt.
Serve with rice – a Sümi Naga mixed-vegetable preparation.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Hearty vegetarian option using local tubers and bamboo shoot.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Thick, comforting consistency.

title: Hinkeju (Mixed Boiled Vegetables)
steps: Boil or steam a mixture of available seasonal vegetables and greens with minimal seasoning.
Serve as a simple side with rice and a meat dish or chutney.
Everyday vegetable component of a Naga meal.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal local greens, beans, pumpkin, etc.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Naga meals almost always include boiled or steamed vegetables alongside meat and rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Freshness of the produce is key.

title: Sticky Rice / Ashetsang
steps: Soak and steam sticky rice until soft and translucent.
Eat plain, lightly salted, or slightly sweetened as a snack or side.
Common across many Naga communities.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple steamed sticky rice – versatile as snack or accompaniment.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often carried for journeys or field work.
